solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uproar about cryptics being cut back

parts.note: about, as in a rumour being about, means out

indicators.note: the word cryptics is cut down heavily from its back end, leaving only its opening letters

explanation.surface: Solvers complain loudly that the paper is printing fewer puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link word but supplies OUT, as in a rumour being out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a public clamour of protest, a synonym for uproar.

clue.text: Launches into reason for 27?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: read as zero pens, pens that draw noughts, which cause the O inking that the 27 answer splits into

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the 27 answer can be split O INKING, and 0 PENS would cause it.
explanation.definitionFit: To open something is to begin it, as one launches into a speech.

clue.text: Scold, in time, one for cooking the books

parts.note: a term is a period of time
an Aga is a brand of kitchen range cooker
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An accountant fiddling the books is rebuked in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking the books' suggests fraud; here 'one for cooking' is an Aga and 'the books' NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing woman, one who scolds.

clue.text: Game personnel in industrial heartland

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game
HR is human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: Sports staff work in a manufacturing region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr valley in western Germany is that country's historic centre of coal and steel production.

clue.text: Apropos hoax, laugh, oddly reflecting "we'd give it a whirl!"

indicators.note: reflecting means the picked letters are read back to front, like a mirror image
oddly here takes alternate letters of the three words, the ones in the even positions

explanation.surface: A gossipy remark about a hoax and a laugh, followed by a cheerful exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'Apropos hoax, laugh' (P,O,O,H,A,L,U,H) read backwards under 'reflecting' give HULAHOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hula hoop is a plastic ring that a child whirls around the waist, so it could speak of being given a whirl.

clue.text: Group of countries meeting slight problem separate

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a hitch is a minor snag

explanation.surface: A meeting of nations hits a small difficulty and splits up.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or detach, as a trailer from a car.

clue.text: Pops out with Laurel for numerous functions

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A father goes out with Stan Laurel for many engagements.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-purpose is suitable for many different uses.

clue.text: Demanding to have top lowered, is obliged

indicators.note: the top letter of the word for demanding drops down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: tough means demanding, hard

explanation.surface: A demanding boss is forced to take things down a notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought expresses duty, as in being bound or required to do something.

clue.text: Correspondent's twenty-four hours in federal jail to finish

parts.note: a pen is short for a penitentiary, a federal jail in the US
FRI is Friday, a day
end means finish

explanation.surface: A reporter does a day in a federal jail to complete a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'federal jail' is a US penitentiary, known as a pen; 'in' here is only a link, and the 's joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen friend is someone you exchange letters with, a regular correspondent.

clue.text: Short promotion by female that features in build-up

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for promotion is cut off

parts.note: hype is extravagant publicity
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A brief publicity campaign by a woman forms part of a build-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'build-up' is a hyphenated word, so it features the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The short dash joining the two halves of build-up is a hyphen, a punctuation mark.

clue.text: Chance you usually won't have material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the idiom 'not an ...', meaning no chance at all
second meaning: of this world rather than spiritual

explanation.walkthrough: 'You haven't an earthly' is an idiom for having no chance whatever.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly describes worldly, physical things as opposed to heavenly ones, and also the chance in the idiom 'not an earthly'.

clue.text: I say ring for the blessed commander!

definitions.note: I, the symbol for iodine, for example; say signals an example

parts.note: a halo is the ring of light drawn around a saint's head
GEN is the abbreviation for general, a military commander

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise as a saintly commander receives a halo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an exclamation, but it means I (iodine), for example: iodine is a halogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine, chemical symbol I, is one of the halogen elements, so I is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Extended call for peace involving a foreign ruler

indicators.note: involving means the one word wraps round the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet; SHH is the extended version

explanation.surface: A long plea for peace that involves a foreign leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran, a ruler from abroad.

clue.text: Athlete, exhausted and quiet, having not qualified

parts.note: shot means worn out, exhausted
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
utter means absolute, without qualification

explanation.surface: A worn-out sportsman stays quiet after failing to qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field-event competitor who throws the heavy ball.

clue.text: Violent confrontation to experience: I'm slapped on the face

parts.note: afters is slang for a fight that follows, a violent confrontation
to have something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Someone faces a fight and gets slapped in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is slang, chiefly footballing, for a scuffle after a foul; it usually means dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave lotion is splashed or patted onto the cheeks after shaving, so it is slapped on the face.

clue.text: Winger having edge on kid

indicators.note: on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: to kid is to tease, which is to chaff
to edge forward is to inch

explanation.surface: A football winger has the edge on a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch, a bird with wings, hence a winger.

clue.text: One often hailed as the new Verdi in California — British!

indicators.note: in means the rearranged name goes inside the other letters

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: new means the letters of the composer's name are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new Verdi has turned up in California, and he's British!
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's rearranged name sits inside the British abbreviation rather than after it, splitting B from R.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi drivers are flagged down in the street, so they are hailed by passengers.

clue.text: Thus having easily passed acid test, getting buzz

parts.note: pH is the scale on which acidity is tested
a pH of one is strongly acidic, easily passing as acid

explanation.surface: Someone sails through a stringent test and gets a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: A substance at pH 1 would easily pass any test for acidity.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a buzz is informal for to call them on the telephone.

clue.text: In agreement lasting sixty seconds, dissent's beginning

parts.note: of one min, short for minute, is sixty seconds long

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word dissent's

explanation.surface: Agreement holds for a minute before dissent starts.
explanation.definitionFit: People of one mind are unanimous, holding the same opinion.

clue.text: Bill after turning from gas is steep

indicators.note: after turning means the word for bill is turned round

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab
HE is the chemical symbol for helium, a gas

explanation.surface: A bill arrives after a gas supply was switched off, and it is steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an expensive bill, but it is the verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it in liquid, much as one would bathe it.

clue.text: Dicky this time is buttonholed by club bore

indicators.note: buttonholed means caught and held, so the letters sit inside the club

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or faulty, so the letters of this are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tedious golfer corners someone at the club to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear, endured.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is the past tense of bear, meaning endured, the same as withstood.

clue.text: Furniture item that now needs repair

indicators.note: needs repair means the letters are broken and must be put back together differently

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is now in need of mending.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatnot is a stand with open shelves for displaying ornaments, an item of furniture.

clue.text: What's for watching you might think outside

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for the television set
second meaning: from the idiom think outside ..., meaning be creative

explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for television; 'think outside the box' means think unconventionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage calls a television set this, and the idiom for creative thinking uses the same phrase.

clue.text: Put back in control, thanks primarily to our boss?

parts.note: reins are what a rider controls a horse with
ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the following word to

parts.note: ED is the editor, the boss of the newspaper staff who set the puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone is restored to power, thanks mainly to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our boss' is the newspaper's editor, ED. The definition stops at 'Put back in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate someone is to restore them to a former position or office.

clue.text: N African king's daughter embraced by goddess

indicators.note: embraced by means the daughter's letter is held inside the goddess's name

parts.note: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A king's daughter is hugged by a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris I was the first and only king of Libya, reigning from 1951 to 1969.

clue.text: Shark fighters in Jaws: film replacing a western

indicators.note: replacing means the film's title takes the place of the other letters in the word Jaws

parts.note: the letter A plus W, short for western
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: Fighters of sharks appear in a film where another movie replaces a western.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jets and the Sharks are the rival gangs in West Side Story, so they fight each other.
explanation.definitionFit: In the musical West Side Story the Jets are the gang who battle the rival Sharks.

clue.text: Ducks out of mounting charity events around university

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes round the letter for university
mounting means the word goes upwards, read in reverse in this down entry

parts.note: rags are British student fundraising events for charity

explanation.surface: Ducks drop out of rising charity events at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like birds, but it is a term of endearment, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck and sugar are both affectionate terms of address, like darling, used in parts of Britain.

clue.text: Maybe miss a year's events, all but the last

indicators.note: all but the last means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an annal is the record of a single year's events

explanation.surface: Someone may skip a year's activities, all except the final one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' is not the verb; it means a girl, and the answer is an example of a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a girl's name, so it is an example of a young woman, a miss.

clue.text: Plant that's excessively puffed up, but not round

indicators.note: but not tells us the round letter is dropped from the word for excessively

parts.note: over means too much, excessively
O is round in shape
vain means conceited, puffed up

explanation.surface: A plant that is extremely proud of itself, though not plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain is a herb of the verbena genus, a flowering plant once used in folk medicine.

clue.text: So the swine's going back to work, protecting home and family

indicators.note: protecting means the reversed word guards the other pieces inside it
back means the word for work is reversed

parts.note: to go is to work, as when a machine goes
in means at home
kin are family

explanation.surface: A pig returns to work, sheltering its home and family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So the swine's going' means that is how the pig sounds; 'going' is its noise, not its departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting noise a pig makes, the way a swine goes.

clue.text: Romantic poet translated stories about the heart in Latin

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other letter
translated means the letters of stories are converted into a new order
the heart in picks the central letter of the word Latin

explanation.surface: A Romantic poet's tales are rendered around the core of a Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and his sister Christina, were Victorian poets in the Romantic tradition.

clue.text: Swimmer, one you catch sleeping with leading lady

parts.note: Z, a snore written down, is what you catch from someone sleeping
and means with, together
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: A man is caught sleeping with the star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests an actress; it is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The zander is a freshwater fish of the perch family, a creature that lives in water.
